entries.label: Forks
entries.description: Fork — one piece attacks two or more enemy pieces at once, so your opponent can only save one.

entries.label: Pins
entries.description: Pin — an enemy piece cannot move (or should not) because a more valuable piece sits behind it.

entries.label: Skewers
entries.description: Skewer — you attack a valuable piece; when it moves away, you win the piece behind it.

entries.label: Discovered attacks
entries.description: Discovered attack — you move one piece out of the way and uncover an attack from the piece behind it.

entries.label: Double check
entries.description: Double check — two pieces give check at the same time, so the king has to move.

entries.label: X-ray
entries.description: X-ray — a piece attacks or defends a square "through" an enemy piece that is standing in the way.

entries.label: Free pieces
entries.description: Free pieces — an enemy piece is left without enough protection, so you can simply win it.

entries.label: Trapped pieces
entries.description: Trapped piece — an enemy piece has no safe square to go to, so you can win it.

entries.label: Removing the defender
entries.description: Removing the defender — take or chase away the piece that protects something, then win what it was guarding.

entries.label: Deflection
entries.description: Deflection — force an enemy piece away from an important job, like guarding a square or another piece.

entries.label: Attraction
entries.description: Attraction — lure an enemy piece (often the king) onto a square where you can hit it.

entries.label: Clearing the way
entries.description: Clearance — move a piece away on purpose so another one of your pieces can use the square or the line.

entries.label: Interference
entries.description: Interference — put a piece between two enemy pieces to cut the link between them.

entries.label: In-between move (zwischenzug)
entries.description: In-between move — instead of the move everyone expects, you first play a surprising check or threat.

entries.label: Quiet move
entries.description: Quiet move — a calm move with no check and no capture that sets up a threat the opponent cannot stop.

entries.label: Mate in 1
entries.description: Mate in 1 — you can checkmate the king with your very next move.

entries.label: Mate in 2
entries.description: Mate in 2 — you checkmate the king in two moves, whatever your opponent does in between.

entries.label: Mate in 3
entries.description: Mate in 3 — you checkmate the king in three moves, whatever your opponent does in between.

entries.label: Back-rank mate
entries.description: Back-rank mate — a rook or queen checkmates a king that is stuck behind its own pawns on the edge row.

entries.label: Smothered mate
entries.description: Smothered mate — a knight checkmates a king that is completely surrounded by its own pieces.

entries.label: Arabian mate
entries.description: Arabian mate — a rook and a knight team up to checkmate a king in the corner.

entries.label: Anastasia's mate
entries.description: Anastasia's mate — a knight and a rook trap the king against the edge of the board.

entries.label: Boden's mate
entries.description: Boden's mate — two bishops on crossing diagonals checkmate a king boxed in by its own pieces.

entries.label: Hook mate
entries.description: Hook mate — a rook, a knight and a pawn work together to checkmate the king.

entries.label: Two-bishop mate
entries.description: Two-bishop mate — both of your bishops cover the escape squares and deliver checkmate.

entries.label: Sacrifices
entries.description: Sacrifice — you give up material on purpose to get something bigger back, like a winning attack.

entries.label: Attack on f2/f7
entries.description: Attack on f2/f7 — the squares next to the king at the start of the game (f2 for White, f7 for Black) are the weakest.

entries.label: Exposed king
entries.description: Exposed king — the enemy king has little cover around it, which makes attacks against it strong.

entries.label: Attack on the kingside
entries.description: Kingside attack — you go after an enemy king that has castled on the short side, near the h-file.

entries.label: Attack on the queenside
entries.description: Queenside attack — you go after an enemy king that has castled on the long side, near the a-file.

entries.label: Finding the defence
entries.description: Defence — your opponent is threatening something, and you must find the move that keeps you safe.

entries.label: Zugzwang
entries.description: Zugzwang — it is your opponent's turn, and every move they can make makes their position worse.

entries.label: Endgames (mixed)
entries.description: Endgame — only a few pieces are left, so every single move counts.

entries.label: Pawn endgames
entries.description: Pawn endgame — only kings and pawns are left, so it is all about pawns and king moves.

entries.label: Rook endgames
entries.description: Rook endgame — rooks (and pawns) are the only pieces left besides the kings.

entries.label: Bishop endgames
entries.description: Bishop endgame — bishops (and pawns) are the only pieces left besides the kings.

entries.label: Knight endgames
entries.description: Knight endgame — knights (and pawns) are the only pieces left besides the kings.

entries.label: Queen endgames
entries.description: Queen endgame — queens (and pawns) are the only pieces left besides the kings.

entries.label: Advanced pawns
entries.description: Advanced pawn — a pawn that is close to the last row can decide the game.

entries.label: Promotion
entries.description: Promotion — push a pawn to the last row and turn it into a queen or another strong piece.

entries.label: Opening tactics
entries.description: Opening tactics — tricks that come up in the first moves of the game.

entries.label: Middlegame tactics
entries.description: Middlegame tactics — tricks in the busy part of the game, when most pieces are still on the board.

entries.label: Punish the mistake
entries.description: Punish the mistake — your opponent just slipped, so find the move that wins big.

entries.label: Get an advantage
entries.description: Advantage — find the move that leaves you clearly better.

entries.label: London System puzzles
entries.description: Puzzles from real games that began like your London System (White plays d4 and Bf4).

entries.label: Caro-Kann Defence puzzles
entries.description: Puzzles from real games that began like your Caro-Kann Defence (Black answers e4 with ...c6).

entries.label: Slav Defence puzzles
entries.description: Puzzles from real games that began like your Slav Defence (Black answers d4 and c4 with ...d5 and ...c6).
